decisions.reason: As a multi-item supplement range with an early standalone presentation and a very close fit to the firm's consumer-health portfolio expansion, prior investment and public commitment strongly favor continuation.

This visibly launched skin-and-hair supplement remains well aligned with the firm's broaden-the-portfolio strategy, so sunk launch costs and the ease of blaming weaker results on temporary demand fluctuations support keeping it.

Although it was less prominently promoted than A or B, it still extends the established supplement line, and escalation of commitment makes management more likely to persist than to admit the product has disappointed.

Despite being more distant from the legacy offer, the OTC migraine tablet involved a visible launch and supports the announced move into new consumer-health products, so management would usually continue it unless poor results were unmistakable.
